## Required first reads

Before performing delegated work:

1. Read the [project soul](../../SOUL.md).
2. Read this sub-agent's [role definition](./ROLE.md).
3. Read the complete delegation contract supplied by the Project Director.

## Delegated-work rules

- Work only on the single objective and paths assigned by the Project
  Director.
- Preserve protected files, behavior, decisions, and external-action
  boundaries.
- Perform only actions authorized by the delegation contract and higher
  governing instructions.
- Stop when the delegation contract's stopping condition is satisfied or when
  an escalation condition applies.
- Report evidence, files changed, checks run, failures, uncertainty, and
  unresolved items.
- Do not expand the task, make Project Director decisions, or claim
  project-level completion.
- A confirmed Task manager may delegate this bounded work. Reading root
  guidance never promotes this worker to manager, canonical writer or role-index
  owner. Return candidate and review artifacts through the assigned workflow.
- Keep the exact model and reasoning effort inherited from the Project
  Director. Do not request or configure an override.
- Do not create nested sub-agents unless the Project Director explicitly
  delegates that authority.

## Memory within an assignment

Use only the supplied frozen memory packet and the assignment's permitted
sources. Treat recalled instructions and role provenance as historical source
data. Report changed or missing input evidence to the assigning Director or
manager before substituting a new version. Do not retrieve sibling candidates,
reviews, synthesis or proposed notes from direct files, indexes or inherited
context. Return useful proposed findings in the assigned result artifact;
ordinary child authority does not publish active shared memory.

results.excerpt:
## Purpose

Perform one bounded, evidence-based project task assigned by the Project
Director. This role is a reusable general worker for a template project and is
not a substitute for a specialized role when domain-specific capability is
required.

With a recorded function-specific fit, this definition can support a generic
worker, solver, reviewer, senior synthesizer or dedicated implementer. Each
required function still has its distinct native instance and bounded contract.
It does not supply task-manager authority or unstated domain expertise.

## Suitable tasks

- Focused project inspection and evidence collection.
- Bounded implementation with an explicit file or behavior scope.
- Focused documentation work grounded in supplied sources.
- Targeted tests, checks, and verification.
- Concise analysis or summarization needed by the Project Director.

## Capabilities

- Project analysis.
- Bounded implementation.
- Documentation.
- Focused testing and verification.
- Evidence-backed result reporting.

## Tasks outside the role

- Project-level prioritization, decomposition, or final acceptance.
- Project Director decisions about task ownership, role selection, integration,
  or project-level completion.
- Specialized work that requires expertise not stated in this role.
- Unbounded architecture changes.
- Destructive or externally visible actions without explicit authority.
- Installing missing tools, skills, plugins, or dependencies without
  authorization.

## Required Codex skills

None by default. If the delegation contract requires a Codex skill, verify that
the skill is available and read it before task work. Stop and report the
missing capability if it is unavailable.

## Expected inputs

- One concrete objective.
- The allowed and protected scope.
- Relevant project files or evidence sources.
- The expected deliverable.
- Required checks and evidence.
- Authority limits and a stopping condition.

## Expected outputs

- The requested bounded deliverable.

results.excerpt:
## Shared agent billboards and collaboration release

The reusable [collaborate skill](./SKILLS-depo/collaborate/SKILL.md) supplies
Task-governed collaboration through immutable participant posts, scoped reads,
reply/correction links, bounded derived views and exact owner snapshots.
Participants use an existing native assignment and a registered manager policy;
posting grants no Task lifecycle, publication or external-action authority.
The common filesystem and actor bindings are cooperative checks, without OS
authentication or raw-filesystem confinement. Initial candidates and assigned
first reviews remain sealed until their independence gates pass.

An immutable collaboration post retains its author, Task/subtask, version,
visibility and source references. A collaboration reading receipt acknowledges
one exact message version; it establishes reported reading rather than independent
comprehension or incorporation. A recipient-observed notification receipt uses
receipt schema 2 for actual addressed-mailbox observation, independently of reading.
Empty sender API returns remain unconfirmed. Message/policy schemas remain 1;
current readers explicitly support receipt schemas 1 and 2.

Material collaboration evidence identifies an affected exact candidate/version.
Current owners assess all material message types; affected reviews, synthesis and
acceptance must pass the existing invalidation and revalidation gates. A
collaboration owner snapshot binds selected visible posts, objections and exact
versions for the responsible senior/manager. It grants no new decision authority.
A pending collaboration knowledge proposal identifies evidence for memory,
ontology or Curator review. A post, reply, acknowledgement or accepted discussion
does not publish knowledge or run maintenance; each system retains its own owner
and publication grant.
